Brain scans have shown that dogs process words using similar mechanisms to humans — including both left-hemisphere word meaning processing and right-hemisphere intonation processing — and they can distinguish between familiar and unfamiliar words, including foreign languages [d3][d2][d8]. However, some experts and studies take a more nuanced view: one source notes that dogs essentially memorize and associate frequently used vocables with meanings rather than truly comprehending human language broadly [d6], and another argues that dogs are not naturally attuned to human speech and that expecting them to understand it may be unrealistic [d9].
